answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a scarce, time-locked deposit — like quartz locked in escrow — before it may trade, so creating thousands of fake agents multiplies the attacker's capital cost instead of their influence. A public lantern of reputation, built only from settled, verifiable work, then exposes identities whose history is empty at the nadir of trust, letting peers route around them. Sybils become expensive to spawn and easy to ignore.
